plan.english: Dog, guard the sheep! Do not leave the lambs! The wolf comes by night. Do you hear? I see the wolf's eyes. Then the dog stood up and ran forth, and the wild beast fled.
Cattle, come to the cow-stall! The sun has sunk, and night is coming. Drink! Then the herdsman leads the herd home, and the dog follows. They lie in the cow-stall.
Wife, where are the lambs? The lambs are in the pasture. I saw them, and they were eating. Then the son guards them. Come, wife, let us eat.
Day dawned. Then the herdsman drove the herd to the pasture. The herd was eating. Then he sat down and kept looking at the herd. Then he saw the wolf and cried out, and drove it out.
Sister, milk the sheep! Brother, the lambs are sated. I am milking them. Bring the beer! The parent heard the sister's voice.
In the night a wild beast came. The pigs became afraid, and the horses trembled. Then the father stood up and cried: Son, drive the wolf out! Then it fled.
The herdsman's herd is great. His own horse is swift. No beast seized his sheep. May his fame be good, and may his fame be imperishable!
Sheep, eat on the hill and drink at the river! Do not be afraid! The dog protects you. May your wool grow, and may your lambs live! Then I shall lead you home.

Stranger, who are you? I am a herdsman. Where did you come from? I came from the mountain. Is your herd large? My herd is large, but the pasture has dried up. Go to my pasture, stranger, and let us eat.
King, ten cattle are missing. I looked for them on the mountain. Then the son tracked, and I found them by the river. Seven are alive, and the wolf devoured three.

It rained. The herdsman did not drive the herd to the pasture. They were lying in the cow-stall. He sat at the hearth and drank beer. The fire was burning. Then the woman twisted the wool. The rain-cloud went away.
Father Sky, protect our herd! May the beast not seize the sheep, nor a stranger steal the horses. May it eat in the pasture, and may it be sated. Hear our word!
Brother, look! I see a snake by the river. The snake creeps. Do not seize it! The dog will kill it. Are you afraid? I am not afraid.
Let us drive the herd to the hill. There is a lake there. The son will follow the herd, and the brother will stand guard. Grandson, remember! Do not go astray on the hill.
Yoke the two horses! Plough the arable land! Pull the yoke, horses! Toil, man, toil! The earth is split. Mother Earth, grow rich! The wage is good.
Twist the wool! Stretch the string! The woman twists the wool and stretches the string. Listen to the woman's voice! What did the woman make? She made a string.
Pull, men! Push, men! The wheel turns. The wagon goes forward. The heart is strong. Do not stand still!
Boil, beer, boil! The fire burns. Cook the beer for the guest! The guest sips, and the heart became joyful. Dear one, drink, and be sated!
Smith, heat the awl! Straighten the awl in the fire! The fire is burning. Strike, smith, strike! The awl is good. The smith's fame is great.
Stand, cattle, stand! The woman milks. Give, cattle, give! The lamb sips. Do not be afraid! Be joyful, woman!
Build the house, build it! Put the house in order! Brothers, pull! The house stands, and the hearth burns. Brothers, take your wage!
Carry the water from the river, men! Sister, carry the water from the lake. The lake has become cold. Give beer to the guest! Do not slip! Keep carrying!
Smear the wheel with pitch! Turn the wheel! The pitch is burning. The craftsman built the wheel. The wheel is good. The chariot is light.
We go to the hill. The dog goes forward, and we follow. Let us go!
Sheep, stand! We cut the wool. Dry the wool by the fire! Now you are naked.
Split the rock, men! Split it! We sweat. The rock breaks. Do not slip!
Be awake, son, be awake! It is getting dark. Look at the herd! Listen to the voice! Do not lie down.
When Dawn is red, the rain-cloud comes. When Dawn comes bright, it does not rain. When the night turns cold, the sky grows bright. The herdsman sees the dawn.
When a cloud sits on the hill, it rains. When mist lies on the lake, it does not rain. The rain-cloud comes from the mountain and covers the arable land. The wind leads the cloud.
The wind blows. When a strong wind blows, the clouds flee. When the wind lies down, the lake lies flat. The voice of the wind is great. Wind and rain-cloud are brothers.
When the cattle lie down, the rain-cloud comes. When the horses tremble, Perkwunos arrives. When the pigs are afraid, the wind blows. When the wolf cries out, the night grows cold.
When Perkwunos speaks, the earth drinks the water. Perkwunos hurled fire from the cloud. Perkwunos, split the cloud and give us rain! Father Sky, may it rain!
When the sun sinks, it grows dark. When the sun sinks into cloud, the wind comes. Darkness lies on the hill. The night grows cold.

The rain-cloud gives water. Water nourishes the herd. The herd nourishes the house. The river fills when the rain-cloud arrives. When no rain-cloud comes, the lake dries up, and the beasts are thirsty.
When the sun grows warm, the mist melts. The sun burns the arable land, and the beasts sweat. When the wind grows warm, the snake creeps.

When a rain-cloud arrives, lead the herd to the cow-stall. When a cloud sits on the hill, do not drive the pigs to the mountain. When a strong wind blows, lead the son home. When Perkwunos speaks, sit at the hearth.
Sky is father, Earth is mother. The rain-cloud is the offspring of Sky. Mother Earth, feed the cattle! Father Sky, give water! Both are dear.
When the rain-cloud comes, do not plough. When the cloud has gone, the earth drinks, and the arable land is rich. When the rain-cloud does not come, the man seeks a river.
Rain-cloud, come! May it rain on the arable land! May the wind not break the cow-stall. Rain-cloud, go away! May the sun shine bright.
Who knows the cloud? The father knows the cloud. Who knows the mist? The mother knows the mist. Who knows the wind? The one who has seen knows the wind.
